hints: Focus on the word hot, as chlorine behaves differently with cold dilute NaOH and with hot concentrated NaOH.
Recall that with hot NaOH, chlorine disproportionates to give $\text{Cl}^-$ and $\text{ClO}_3^-$, so work out the oxidation state in each ion.
Check which of -1, +3 and +1 actually appear in those two products, remembering that +1 belongs to the cold reaction.
walkthrough:
**Recognise disproportionation**

Chlorine starts at oxidation state 0 in $\text{Cl}_2$. With NaOH it is both reduced and oxidised at the same time. This is called disproportionation.

$$\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{Cl}^- + \text{ClO}_x^-$$

**Write the hot NaOH equation**

Cold dilute NaOH gives chlorate(I), $\text{NaClO}$. Hot concentrated NaOH gives chlorate(V), $\text{NaClO}_3$. Learn this difference carefully.

$$3\text{Cl}_2 + 6\text{NaOH} \rightarrow 5\text{NaCl} + \text{NaClO}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Assign oxidation states in products**

In $\text{NaCl}$, Na is +1 so Cl must be -1. In $\text{NaClO}_3$, Na is +1 and each O is -2, so Cl must be +5 to balance.

$$+1 + \text{Cl} + 3(-2) = 0 \text{ so Cl} = +5$$

**Match to statements 1, 2 and 3**

Statement 1 (-1) is present in $\text{NaCl}$. Statement 3 (+1) is only for the cold reaction product $\text{NaClO}$. Statement 2 (+3) is not formed at all. The +5 state is formed but is not listed.

So only 1 is correct.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Only -1 is formed in the hot reaction. +1 is the cold product ($\text{ClO}^-$) and +3 is not formed in either reaction.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean 1 and 2 are correct. While -1 is correct for $\text{Cl}^-$, +3 is wrong. The oxidised product with hot NaOH is $\text{ClO}_3^-$ where Cl is +5, not +3.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean 2 and 3 are correct. Neither +3 nor +1 is formed with hot NaOH. +1 comes from the cold dilute NaOH reaction to make $\text{NaClO}$, a common trap if you miss the word hot.
options.D: Correct. This means 1 only is correct. Hot NaOH gives $\text{NaCl}$ containing Cl(-1) and $\text{NaClO}_3$ containing Cl(+5). Of the three listed states, only -1 appears.
